pr_title: boot: load device tree even if no original config exists
pr_body:
Firmware may not have loaded a devicetree, for example if the device
shipped with windows and exclusively supports ACPI.
We should always load the specified devicetree regardless of firmware
state to enable booting on platforms where Linux only supports DT.

Fixes #24059

cc @daniel-thompson, since you wrote this and I just rebased / tested.

issue_context.title: Boot Loader Entry Key `devicetree` Unsupported
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

251.3

### Used distribution

Arch Linux

### Linux kernel version used

5.19 (rc1)

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

aarch64

### Component

systemd-boot

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

Should be jumping to the kernel.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25991564/179630230-65f9bdfa-2a14-4b5c-8e41-4768d7a5e686.png)


### Steps to reproduce the problem

Create an aarch64 archiso for the Lenovo ThinkPad X13s, like done here: https://github.com/ironrobin/archiso-x13s
Flash the ISO to a USB drive.
Boot into the USB drive.
Select an entry that looks something like this:
```
title   Arch Linux install medium (aarch64, UEFI)
linux      /arch/boot/aarch64/Image
devicetree /arch/boot/aarch64/sc8280xp-thinkpad.dtb
initrd     /arch/boot/aarch64/initramfs-linux.img
options archisobasedir=arch archisolabel=ARCH_AARCH64_202207 efi=novamap clk_ignore_unused console=tty0
```
Note: Things work if you use the `dtb=` kernel option in the options list. Yet if you use `devicetree` Entry Key it is showing as Unsupported. 

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

_No response_
comments: This means your firmware does not support the device tree fixup protocol, which sd-boot relies upon for device tree support. (`dtb=` cmdline is handled directly by the kernel and therefore works)

@medhefgo
Others with the same machine/kernel/dtb combination are reporting that GRUB2 devicetree command works just fine. So, shouldn't sd-boot do whatever GRUB2 is doing in case that protocol isn't available? If protocol isn't supported, it should just skip that step.

@theironrobin that would mean we'd have to embedd an ftd stack, which we really don't want.

See https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/19417 for details of the discussion.
@poettering Do you suggest just using GRUB2 on ARM64 devices, then?
I am not experienced in the arm64 world. Is there no perspective on getting the dt fixup protocol into place in your environment?

in the vendor provided fw, unlikely.

I didn't quite get why lack of fixup proto would require full fdt stack.. from a quick look at the proto, it was just patching an already loaded dt.  So if the proto wasn't supported couldn't you just skip that?

@robclark I've been trying to figure that out too. As far as I can tell fixups are skipped with a warning and a 3s stall: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/9e6df034128936895df2d6348eefce61317ebcc2/src/boot/efi/devicetree.c#L44-L47 So it doesn't seem like the lack of the fixup protocol is causing this error... please note that I've only looked at that very briefly.

I think they theory of failure here is wrong. sd-boot hasn't reported Unsupported because there is no fixup protocol, it has reported Unsupported because it cannot find any DT (e.g. right at the beginning on devicetree_install()).

Currently I think sd-boot only supports updating the DT on systems that *already* have a DT present. For the QCom laptops (which are ACPI by default) there is no existing DT and it gives up:
https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/9e6df034128936895df2d6348eefce61317ebcc2/src/boot/efi/devicetree.c#L84-L86

![00baf46d-8fc9-4e91-9f59-fcfb5a6dc610](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/110067826/181870493-0f3e8bc4-84ec-4f41-801b-478097437706.jpg)

someone tell me what I can do here (enter a usb memory with linux and I get this)

@daniel-thompson I rebased this patch onto v254, and it got sd-boot working on the x13s (there's a message about not being able to find the fixup protocol, but it's not fatal).

I don't know enough about sd-boot to know what the implications of this patch are for other systems... or was this experiment meant to just confirm that the actual problem is with finding the DT?

> @daniel-thompson I rebased this patch onto v254, and it got sd-boot working on the x13s (there's a message about not being able to find the fixup protocol, but it's not fatal).

Awesome, thanks for testing it.

> I don't know enough about sd-boot to know what the implications of this patch are for other systems... or was this experiment meant to just confirm that the actual problem is with finding the DT?

To be honest I had completely forgotten about sending this so I can't be entirely sure. It's a pretty conservative change so I wouldn't expect problems with other systems. (although we should definitely remove the line that @bluca picked up on in review).

review_comments:
Nitpicking but this comment is justifying why we deleted the (broken) error path rather than what the code is actually doing. How about something more like the following (which, among other things, hints that we did check how the InstallConfigurationTable() in devicetree_cleanup() actually works):

Capture the original value for the devicetree table. NULL is not an error in this case so we don't need to check the return value. NULL simply means the system fw had no devicetree initially (and is the correct value to use to return to the initial state if needed).
sure whatever, I've already spend far too much time on a simple patch that someone else wrote to fix sd-boot on these platforms 😓
This check should stay, and a debug level log be written, instead of returning (same below)
we have no debug logging currentl in EFI mode. log_trace probably comes closest

If there can't be a debug message here then maybe no message is best.

We were told to install a devicetree and we installed one. I'm not sure there is a need for more "drama" if we install a devicetree on a system without a DT than a system with an existing DT.
+1 for this, installing a DT should not implicitly depend on whatever environment the EFI firmware provides, it's intentional - and if not then usually a pretty obvious thing to spot.
